Recommended: Examples: bean chili or stew with added cheese; noodle or rice stir-fries with meat/seafood and vegetables (cooked with oil); lasagna or pasta bake with extra cheese and creamy sauces; add butter to cooked veggies and potatoes; curries with added coconut milk or cream and extra legumes. Addresses: weight loss, low appetite. Context: High-calorie dinner suggestions for weight gain.

do_recommend: Examples: full-fat Greek yogurt with honey and nuts; trifle or mousse; rice pudding with whole milk; milkshakes or ice cream; even avocado chocolate mousse as a nutrient-dense dessert

clinical_context: Guidance for patients with dysphagia or post-esophagectomy on making foods easier to swallow
key_recommendation: Modify food textures (purée or mince as needed) and use proper techniques (chew thoroughly, eat slowly, add moisture) to aid swallowing
do_recommend: Purée or finely mince foods; chew well; eat slowly; use gravies, sauces, or fluids to moisten foods
avoid_recommend: Avoid drinking through straws (to reduce air swallowing); avoid carbonated drinks if they cause discomfort
notes: OPA advice for managing swallowing difficulties

Context: Guidance for patients with dysphagia or post-esophagectomy on making foods easier to swallow.

clinical_context: Eating strategy for post-esophagectomy or those with reduced stomach capacity
key_recommendation: Have 5-6 small meals a day and time fluids around meals to maximize intake and comfort
do_recommend: Eat ~5-6 small meals or snacks daily instead of large meals
avoid_recommend: Avoid drinking fluids 30 minutes before or after meals if dumping syndrome is an issue (prevents feeling too full from liquids)
notes: OPA advice aligning with standard post-gastrectomy/dumping syndrome guidance

Context: Eating strategy for post-esophagectomy or those with reduced stomach capacity.

clinical_context: Diet adjustments to prevent rapid gastric emptying (dumping syndrome) after stomach surgery
key_recommendation: Slow digestion by including protein/fat in meals and limiting concentrated sugars; consider posture (sometimes lying down after eating can help)
do_recommend: Include protein and healthy fats with meals to slow digestion; choose whole fruit over juice; possibly rest after meals to slow gastric emptying (if advised)
avoid_recommend: Avoid high-sugar foods and drinks, which can trigger dumping (e.g., fruit juices, sweets)
notes: OPA advice reflecting common dumping syndrome management techniques

Avoid: Avoid high-sugar foods and drinks that can trigger dumping (e.g., fruit juice, sweets). Addresses: dumping syndrome (post-surgery). Context: Diet adjustments to prevent rapid gastric emptying (dumping syndrome) after stomach surgery.

clinical_context: Lifestyle and diet tips for esophageal cancer patients who experience reflux after surgery
key_recommendation: Use reflux management strategies: eat well before lying down, elevate the upper body when sleeping, and avoid large meals or trigger foods
do_recommend: Finish eating at least 2-3 hours before bedtime; elevate head while sleeping; focus on lean proteins and vegetables in the diet
avoid_recommend: Avoid large meals and known reflux triggers (spicy, acidic, caffeine, chocolate, alcohol, peppermint)
notes: OPA advice for managing reflux post-esophagectomy
embedding_text: Preventing/Treating Reflux – Employ reflux control techniques: allow 2-3 hours after eating before lying down, sleep propped up, avoid big meals or trigger foods. Recommended: Finish eating at least 2-3 hours before bedtime; elevate head while sleeping; focus on lean proteins and vegetables. Avoid: Avoid large meals and known reflux triggers (spicy, acidic, caffeine, chocolate, alcohol, peppermint). Addresses: acid reflux (GERD). Context: Lifestyle and diet tips for esophageal cancer patients who experience reflux after surgery.

advice_category: Emotional and Social Aspects of Eating
clinical_context: Holistic advice addressing the emotional challenges of eating after esophageal surgery
key_recommendation: Maintain social connection and a positive mindset with food: eat with others when possible, focus on tolerable foods, and gradually expand diet without stress
do_recommend: Eat with family or friends to make meals enjoyable; focus on foods you can tolerate and enjoy; try new foods gradually as confidence grows
avoid_recommend: Avoid isolating yourself during meals or feeling guilty about not eating certain foods
notes: OPA emphasizes psychosocial support in nutrition
